hypotheses.reasoning: Checkout was healthy until 14:56. Starting at 14:56:08, AWS S3 (us-east-1) began returning 500 InternalError and 503 ServiceUnavailable to payment-svc's PutObject calls on checkout-artifacts-prod. Payment-svc then failed charges with 'storage write failed' (237, 255, 266, ...), order-service passed that on as a 500, and api-gateway returned 500s. The gateway latencies are long (18–28s) because the aws-sdk kept retrying until its retry quota ran out (244). That is amplification, not the cause. S3 answered with errors instead of hanging, so this is an external outage rather than a dependency timeout. No deploys appear in the logs. The disk, TLS, GC, postgres and redis warnings are routine and unrelated.

The SDK retry storm (75 failed attempts in 60s, plus the 503 'reduce your request rate' throttle) may have made the S3 errors worse and stretched out request latency. But the trigger was S3 itself returning 500s.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the AWS Health/status page for S3 in us-east-1. Make the S3 artifact write in payment-svc async or best-effort: queue it and write it later so the charge doesn't fail. Cap SDK retries and add backoff to stop the long tail at the gateway. If the outage lasts, fail over to another region's bucket.
